title: Hearing music in Birmingham: the Elks hall and the radio
summary: He heard bands only outside the Elks Hall and mostly through the radio under his pillow at night.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What kind of places did you have to hear music because you mentioned that you were too young to actually go in to hear some of these players, but you wanted to hear them. What kind of places did you have, or opportunities did you have to hear live musicians?

Well, in Birmingham and at the school, at the school a lot of bands come through with Earl Hines during those years. And, Earl Hines came back to New York. He'd tell Joe Glaser all about that. And, that's the only place that I actually did hear was in Birmingham. That was at the Elks Place. That's where they said I was too young to get in. So. I used to stand outside and try to look through the windows cause I couldn't get in. And, all the other times, I couldn't, this was just like radio.
I didn't go nowhere. I didn't go out. (Inaudible). That's kind of close.

That's pretty close through my life. I got most of mine through the radio. Every night, when I was in school, I used to sit up there and have that radio on when it's late at night under the pillow, to listen.
And what kinds of things were on the radio at that time that you remember?

Well, I had the big bands that was broadcasting. You know, that was a big time it seems. That was a big time of year that, oh, I'm trying to think of some of the names of some of the bands that used to broadcast. Clyde McCoy, I used to get him a lot. I even had, well, that's doing it, Isham Jones. You know, besides the Duke, and Earl Hines and Louis. Those seem to be some of the main bands that I got at that time, whenever I could.
And then, after I got to 'Bama State, I went to New Orleans. And, that's where I got a lot of things.
